hazard.chemical_contact_hazard: Definition: A hazardous contact pathway involving a chemical substance and a plausible route to a person, such as skin/eye contact, inhalation, ingestion, splash, spray, mist, fumes, or spill contact. Include when: the specified resource is the chemical source, released chemical, contaminated material, or failed containment/pathway that can expose a person; the text describes splash, spray, fumes, vapor, gas, spill contact, or direct body contact with the chemical; the chemical is handled, transferred, opened, disconnected, leaked, or projected in a way that creates an exposure pathway. Exclude when: a chemical is only named, stored, transported, or present without contact, release, or exposure pathway; the resource is emergency shower, eyewash, PPE, hospital, rescue equipment, or another mitigation/context object; the label refers only to the accident outcome; use accident_type chemical_exposure for the human exposure event. Boundary: Resource-specific rule: do not copy this hazard from a chemical to a pump, pipe, valve, or container unless that component is the failed pathway or source of release. Examples: sodium sulfide solution sprayed toward the worker; chlorine gas was released and inhaled.
hazard.corrosive_exposure: Definition: A chemical-contact hazard involving an acidic, alkaline, caustic, or otherwise corrosive substance capable of tissue damage. Include when: acid, alkali, caustic, corrosive, or a clearly corrosive named substance is supported by the text; corrosive liquid, mist, vapor, or residue reaches or can reach a person; chemical burn is linked to the specified corrosive substance or failed containment/pathway. Exclude when: generic chemical exposure without evidence that the substance is corrosive; hot water, steam, flame, or thermal burns without corrosive chemistry; a corrosive substance is merely stored or listed with no exposure pathway. Boundary: Usually coexists with chemical_contact_hazard when both contact pathway and corrosive property are evidenced. Examples: sulfuric acid splashed onto skin; caustic soda solution contacted the employee.
hazard.flammable_or_fire_hazard: Definition: A hazard involving fire, flame, ignition, explosion, explosive atmosphere, combustible dust, or a flammable/explosive material. Include when: fire, flame, ignition, explosion, combustible dust, or flammable vapor/material is described; the specified resource is the fuel, ignition source, explosive material, fire-affected equipment, or failed component in the fire/explosion pathway; hot work ignites nearby flammable material or an explosive atmosphere. Exclude when: hot surfaces, steam, hot water, or temperature burns without ignition/fire evidence; ordinary chemical exposure without flammability or combustion evidence; equipment is present near a fire but not involved in the fire pathway. Boundary: Do not use merely because an event is severe; require fire, ignition, explosion, or flammability evidence. Examples: oil caught fire; flammable vapor ignited during welding.
hazard.high_pressure: Definition: A hazard caused by pressurized liquid, gas, steam, hydraulic pressure, pneumatic pressure, compressed gas, overpressure, or sudden pressure release. Include when: pressure, pressurized line, compressed gas, hydraulic/pneumatic system, boiler, cylinder, or pressure vessel is explicit; rupture, burst, jet, spray, or release is tied to pressure or pressurization; the specified resource contains, generates, transfers, or fails under pressure. Exclude when: ordinary liquid flow, gravity-fed discharge, or generic leak without pressure evidence; stored mechanical energy such as spring/tension/load release without pressure evidence; a pipe, hose, or pump is merely named without pressure-related wording. Boundary: Use stored_energy separately only when a non-pressure stored-energy mechanism is also described. Examples: pressurized line released fluid; compressed-air hose burst.
hazard.rotating_machinery: Definition: A hazard from an energized rotating or spinning part, such as a shaft, belt, pulley, chuck, drill, grinder, roller, fan, rotor, auger, or wheel. Include when: rotation, spinning, moving belt/roller, drill rotation, or rotating machine part is causally involved; body part, clothing, tool, or material is caught by or contacts a rotating component; the specified resource is the rotating part or the machine whose rotating mechanism caused the risk. Exclude when: stationary equipment, disconnected parts, or objects merely falling from equipment; general machinery involvement with no rotating/moving-part evidence; vehicle travel or mobile-equipment movement; use vehicle_mobile_equipment when appropriate. Boundary: Prefer pinch_crush_hazard only when trapping/compression is the main mechanism and rotation is not evidenced. Examples: hand caught in a rotating drill; clothing was pulled into a moving belt.
hazard.pinch_crush_hazard: Definition: A hazard where a person or body part can be trapped, pinched, squeezed, compressed, crushed, or caught between objects or surfaces. Include when: body part caught between two objects, between a moving part and fixed surface, or under a load; load, tool, component, or machine compresses, clamps, pinches, or crushes the person; manual positioning or maintenance creates a caught-between point. Exclude when: a simple struck-by impact with no trapping, compression, or caught-between mechanism; a cut from a sharp object without compression; general pain, strain, or ergonomic injury from lifting without pinch/crush evidence. Boundary: Can coexist with caught_in_between accident type when entrapment/compression is the event. Examples: fingers caught between drilling bar and beam; hand crushed by moving press.
hazard.sharp_object: Definition: A hazard from a sharp edge, blade, tip, point, fragment, burr, shard, cutting tool, or rough metal/glass surface capable of cutting or puncturing. Include when: the specified resource is the blade, knife, sheet edge, broken glass, metal fragment, nail, needle, or cutting source; cut, laceration, puncture, or slicing is linked to a sharp source; broken or fractured material creates a sharp edge that contacts the worker. Exclude when: blunt impact, crushing, burn, or chemical exposure without a cutting source; a wound is mentioned but the sharp resource is not identifiable; ordinary tools or equipment named without sharp-contact evidence. Boundary: Use cut_laceration as the accident_type when the injury event is a cut or puncture. Examples: cut by a metal edge; punctured by a sharp fragment.
hazard.fall_hazard: Definition: A hazard that can cause a person to slip, trip, lose balance, or fall from height or at the same level. Include when: worker slips, trips, stumbles, loses balance, or falls; ladder, platform, scaffold, stairs, floor opening, roof edge, wet floor, or uneven surface is the specified resource causing fall risk; equipment-related fall from or around a machine, vehicle, ladder, platform, or structure. Exclude when: object falls onto a person; use falling_object; pure body movement or same-level trip with no relevant resource signal if the resource is not part of the fall mechanism; fall protection/PPE is only mentioned as mitigation and did not fail. Boundary: For IGDST, keep this only when the resource is part of the fall mechanism, not just because the injury is a fall. Examples: employee fell from a ladder; worker slipped from a platform.
hazard.thermal_hazard: Definition: A hazard from hot or cold material, surface, liquid, steam, molten substance, or temperature extreme that can cause thermal injury. Include when: hot water, steam, hot oil, molten material, heated surface, cold material, or freezing condition contacts or threatens a person; burn, scald, frostbite, or thermal shock is linked to the specified resource; the specified equipment or material is the thermal source or failed pathway of hot/cold release. Exclude when: fire/ignition is the primary mechanism without separate thermal-contact evidence; chemical burns from corrosive substances; use corrosive_exposure and burn as appropriate; a hot process is mentioned but no thermal contact/release pathway is described. Boundary: Thermal hazard is about heat/cold energy; flammable_or_fire_hazard is about ignition/fire/explosion. Examples: hot water caused burns; steam escaped from a line and scalded the worker.
hazard.electrical_hazard: Definition: A hazard involving energized electrical equipment, conductors, voltage, current, arc flash, electric shock, short circuit, or uncontrolled electrical energy. Include when: electric shock, arc, energized wire/cable/panel, live circuit, short circuit, or electrical contact is described; the specified resource is the energized source, conductor, electrical equipment, or failed electrical control; electrical energy contributes to fire, burn, shock, or equipment event. Exclude when: equipment is merely powered or has an electrical component with no electrical-risk evidence; battery or cable is present only as background; mechanical failure of an electrical device without electrical energy involvement. Boundary: Do not infer this label only from resource type; require electrical energy as part of the causal pathway. Examples: contact with energized wire; arc flash from an electrical panel.
hazard.vehicle_mobile_equipment: Definition: A hazard caused by travel, reversing, turning, lifting, hauling, loading, or operation of a vehicle or mobile machine. Include when: truck, forklift, loader, crane, tractor, car, mobile platform, or similar mobile equipment moves, reverses, turns, lifts, or collides; the specified resource is the mobile equipment or the load directly controlled by it; pedestrian struck-by, rollover, collision, or mobile-equipment handling is described. Exclude when: fixed machinery or stationary equipment with no mobile movement; vehicle mentioned only as a location or background object; manual carrying without vehicle/mobile-machine involvement. Boundary: Can pair with collision or struck_by accident types depending on the event. Examples: forklift struck a worker; truck reversed into equipment.
hazard.stored_energy: Definition: A hazard from unexpected release of stored mechanical, gravitational, elastic, hydraulic, pneumatic, or electrical energy, including tension, spring force, suspended loads, rebound, whiplash, residual energy, or sudden release. Include when: object under tension, compression, spring force, suspended load, gravitational potential, residual energy, or rebound releases unexpectedly; blocked, jammed, supported, pressurized, or energized component releases energy during handling or maintenance; the specified resource stores or releases energy that causes movement, impact, ejection, or trapping. Exclude when: ordinary manual force, intended movement, or routine lifting without stored-energy release; generic high-pressure release already captured by explicit high_pressure evidence unless both mechanisms are supported; falling object with no evidence of stored/released energy beyond gravity; use falling_object when simpler. Boundary: This is a broad energy-control concept similar to lockout/tagout reasoning; require a release mechanism. Examples: bar slid from its support; spring-loaded part released suddenly.
hazard.falling_object: Definition: A hazard from an object, load, component, tool, material, or structure dropping, detaching, falling, or being released from above and potentially striking a person. Include when: object, tool, material, component, rock, load, or equipment part falls or drops onto/near a person; the specified resource is the falling source or failed support that releases the falling object; height, overhead work, suspended load, unstable stack, or detachment creates object-fall risk. Exclude when: a person falls; use fall_hazard; horizontal movement, swing, or slide without falling/dropping; object is merely located above but does not fall or detach. Boundary: Use struck_by as accident_type if the falling object hits the person. Examples: rock fell on employee; pipe dropped from a support.

operation_stage.inspection: Definition: Checking, observing, measuring, testing, sampling, troubleshooting, or verifying the condition, quality, or function of a resource. Include when: inspection/check/testing/measurement is the primary activity at the incident moment; the worker is examining a resource before deciding whether to operate, repair, or release it; sampling or monitoring is described as the active task. Exclude when: repair, maintenance, cleaning, installation, or normal operation is the more specific primary activity; the description only says the accident was investigated afterward; inspection is incidental background, not the task being performed. Boundary: If checking immediately turns into corrective work, use repair only when restoration/fixing is the primary action. Examples: during inspection of equipment; while checking the valve condition.
operation_stage.maintenance: Definition: Routine, preventive, or scheduled servicing intended to preserve, adjust, lubricate, calibrate, clean as service, or keep a resource functional. Include when: servicing, preventive maintenance, lubrication, adjustment, calibration, scheduled maintenance, or routine component service is described; the resource is being maintained before failure restoration is needed; the task is maintenance work even if an accident occurs during disassembly or access. Exclude when: corrective restoration after a known failure; use repair; ordinary production or operation with no servicing task; cleaning as a standalone task when cleaning is the clearer stage. Boundary: Maintenance preserves function; repair restores failed/damaged function. Examples: removing a drill rod for maintenance; servicing a conveyor.
operation_stage.cleaning: Definition: Cleaning, washing, flushing, rinsing, clearing, unclogging, scraping, decontaminating, or removing residue from a resource or work area. Include when: cleaning/washing/flushing/clearing residue is the primary activity; the resource is being cleaned, unclogged, purged, or decontaminated; material is removed from equipment specifically to clean it. Exclude when: ordinary handling, transfer, or maintenance without a cleaning action; post-accident cleanup or medical washing as mitigation; routine production where no cleaning task is described. Boundary: Do not use for emergency shower/eyewash use after exposure; those are mitigation context. Examples: cleaning the tank; flushing a pipe before work.
operation_stage.startup: Definition: Starting, activating, energizing, commissioning, restarting, or initiating a machine, process, line, or equipment cycle. Include when: the incident occurs while starting, turning on, energizing, activating, restarting, or commissioning a resource; the process is transitioning from stopped/inactive to running; controls are engaged to initiate operation. Exclude when: equipment is already operating normally; repair or maintenance is the primary activity and startup is not the incident moment; vehicle begins travel as ordinary transport unless startup of equipment is specifically relevant. Boundary: Startup is a transition state, not simply any use of equipment. Examples: during activation of a pump; while starting the machine.
operation_stage.normal_operation: Definition: Routine production, processing, or ordinary use of a resource when no more specific stage explains the incident. Include when: the resource is being operated as intended in routine work; production/process operation is the primary activity and no maintenance, repair, transfer, cleaning, loading, or installation stage is evidenced; phrases such as operating, working with, or during production are the clearest stage evidence. Exclude when: maintenance, repair, cleaning, installation, loading, unloading, transfer, transport, connection/disconnection, or manual handling is more specific; the resource is merely present and no task stage is described; post-accident response or treatment activities. Boundary: Use as a fallback stage only when there is real operation evidence. Examples: while operating the machine; during routine production.
operation_stage.loading: Definition: Placing, charging, filling, feeding, putting, or adding material, goods, components, or substances into a vehicle, container, machine, hopper, tank, line, or storage location. Include when: material is being loaded, filled, charged, fed, or put into a destination resource; the destination or loading equipment is the specified resource; truck/container/tank/machine receives material as the primary activity. Exclude when: removing material; use unloading; moving material between process locations when transfer is clearer; manual lifting/carrying without a destination loading action. Boundary: If both loading and transfer are possible, choose the one emphasized by the action and resource role. Examples: loading ore into a truck; filling a tank with solution.
operation_stage.unloading: Definition: Removing, emptying, extracting, discharging, dumping, or taking material, goods, components, or substances out of a vehicle, container, machine, hopper, tank, or storage location. Include when: material is being unloaded, emptied, discharged, dumped, or removed from a source resource; the source container/vehicle/equipment is the specified resource; the main activity is taking material out rather than putting material in. Exclude when: loading/filling material into a destination; corrective disassembly during repair unless unloading is explicit; planned process flow where transfer is the clearer activity. Boundary: Use transfer for process movement between locations when neither loading nor unloading is the main framing. Examples: unloading bags from a truck; emptying a container.
operation_stage.transfer: Definition: Moving a fluid, gas, chemical, slurry, powder, or material between containers, pipes, tanks, equipment, process lines, or work locations as a process/handling step. Include when: pumping, pouring, draining, conveying, moving, or transferring material between process locations is described; the specified resource is the transferred material or the equipment/pathway used for transfer; fluid/chemical movement through pipe, hose, pump, valve, or container is the primary activity. Exclude when: vehicle travel or hauling as transport; simple manual lifting/carrying without process transfer; loading into or unloading from a vehicle/container when that is more specific. Boundary: Transfer is a process movement concept; transport is vehicle/mobile-equipment movement. Examples: solution transferred through piping; chemical was pumped from one tank to another.
operation_stage.connection_disconnection: Definition: Connecting, coupling, uncoupling, disconnecting, loosening, tightening, opening, closing, removing, or re-establishing a line, hose, cable, fitting, tool, support, guard, or component connection. Include when: worker connects, disconnects, loosens, uncouples, tightens, opens, closes, or removes a connection/fitting/component; hose, pipe, cable, coupling, valve, flange, support, or tool connection is actively manipulated; loss of containment or release occurs during connection/disconnection work. Exclude when: spontaneous breakage, rupture, or detachment with no worker connection action; general repair/maintenance where no connection/disconnection is described; normal operation of already connected equipment. Boundary: Can coexist with maintenance or repair only if both task stage and connection action are explicit. Examples: piping was uncoupled; disconnecting a hose before cleaning.
operation_stage.repair: Definition: Corrective work intended to restore a failed, damaged, broken, jammed, leaking, worn, or malfunctioning resource to service. Include when: fixing, repairing, replacing failed parts, correcting a malfunction, unjamming, or restoring service is described; the resource is already failed/damaged/leaking/malfunctioning before the work; corrective disassembly or replacement is the primary task. Exclude when: preventive/routine servicing without failure evidence; use maintenance; ordinary operation, inspection, or handling with no restoration intent; post-accident medical repair/treatment. Boundary: Repair requires failure/damage or restoration intent; do not infer from any tool use. Examples: repairing the conveyor; replacing a damaged hose.
operation_stage.transport: Definition: Moving people, goods, tools, materials, vehicles, or mobile equipment along a route or between locations, usually by vehicle or mobile machine. Include when: driving, hauling, carrying by truck/forklift/loader, moving between sites, or route travel is described; the specified resource is the vehicle/mobile equipment or transported load central to the event; collision, rollover, reversing, or travel movement occurs during transportation. Exclude when: stationary transfer through pipes, hoses, pumps, conveyors, or process equipment; manual handling without vehicle/mobile-equipment movement; a vehicle is only a parked location or background context. Boundary: Transport is spatial movement by mobile equipment; transfer is process movement of material. Examples: transporting material by truck; forklift moving a load.
operation_stage.installation: Definition: Installing, assembling, mounting, anchoring, positioning, aligning, erecting, or setting up a resource or component for intended use. Include when: resource/component is being installed, mounted, assembled, positioned, aligned, or set up; new equipment, guard, pipe, structure, fixture, or component is being placed into service; installation/assembly activity is the primary stage. Exclude when: removal or replacement during repair unless installation is the main action; ordinary manual positioning without setup-for-use context; routine operation after installation is complete. Boundary: Use manual_handling too only when direct human force/positioning is central and evidenced. Examples: installing a valve; assembling a support structure.
operation_stage.manual_handling: Definition: Direct human lifting, carrying, holding, pulling, pushing, supporting, positioning, manipulating, or restraining a resource or object. Include when: hands, manual force, lifting, carrying, pulling, pushing, holding, or positioning are central to the task; worker manually handles the specified resource or object immediately before the incident; manual support/restraining contributes to caught-between, struck-by, cut, or strain risk. Exclude when: mechanized handling with no direct human manipulation; process transfer/transport where the worker is not manually handling the resource; pure body movement or ergonomic strain with no relevant resource object. Boundary: This stage can coexist with installation, repair, or maintenance if direct manual handling is clearly part of the event. Examples: pulling a bar with both hands; manually positioning a pipe.

accident_type.chemical_splash: Definition: A liquid chemical or solution splashes, sprays, spatters, jets, or is projected onto a person, body part, equipment, or work area. Include when: liquid chemical/solution is sprayed, splashed, projected, jetted, or spattered; the event involves liquid chemical movement from a source/pathway to a person or area; the specified resource is the chemical, failed pathway, or source of splash. Exclude when: gas, vapor, or fumes only without liquid projection; chemical present or leaked away from a person without splash/spray/projection; thermal hot water/steam splash unless chemical nature is evidenced. Boundary: Use chemical_exposure as accident_type too when the splash reaches or affects a person. Examples: sulfide solution was projected; acid splashed into the worker's face.
accident_type.leak_release: Definition: Unintended leakage, spill, escape, discharge, rupture-related release, venting, loss of containment, or uncontrolled release of material or energy. Include when: fluid, gas, chemical, steam, powder, or material leaks, escapes, spills, discharges, or is released unintentionally; container, pipe, hose, valve, pump, vessel, or fitting loses containment; the specified resource is the released material, containment source, or failed release pathway. Exclude when: planned transfer, normal discharge, or intended emptying; chemical/material is present but remains contained; impact/collision/cut event with no released substance or energy. Boundary: Leak_release is an event type; high_pressure or chemical_contact_hazard may be hazards when supported. Examples: piping was uncoupled and liquid escaped; gas leaked from a cylinder.
accident_type.burn: Definition: A thermal or chemical burn, scald, tissue burn, or similar injury caused by heat, hot liquid, steam, flame, electricity, or corrosive chemical. Include when: burn, scald, chemical burn, thermal injury, or equivalent tissue damage is described; hot/cold/chemical/electrical source reaches a person and causes burn injury; the specified resource is the burn source, released material, or failed pathway. Exclude when: exposure without burn/scald/tissue-damage evidence; pain, irritation, or inhalation effects without burn evidence; fire occurs but the described injury/event is not a burn. Boundary: Burn is an injury/event label, not a hazard mechanism by itself. Examples: received burns from hot water; acid caused chemical burns.
accident_type.caught_in_between: Definition: A person or body part becomes caught, trapped, pinched, squeezed, compressed, or crushed between objects or between an object and a fixed surface. Include when: caught, trapped, pinched, compressed, crushed, or squeezed is described; two objects, a moving part and fixed surface, or a load and surface create the event; the specified resource is one of the trapping/crushing objects or failed component. Exclude when: single struck-by impact without entrapment; cut/laceration without caught-between mechanism; manual strain from lifting without trapping/compression. Boundary: Use pinch_crush_hazard for the corresponding hazard mechanism when resource-specific evidence exists. Examples: fingers caught between bar and beam; hand crushed in a press.
accident_type.struck_by: Definition: A person is hit or impacted by a moving, falling, swinging, rolling, detached, thrown, or ejected object. Include when: worker is hit, struck, impacted, knocked, or contacted forcefully by an object/load/component/tool/vehicle; the specified resource is the object that strikes or the equipment causing the strike; falling, swinging, rolling, or ejected object causes impact. Exclude when: caught-between event where trapping/compression is primary; person falls into/onto a surface; use fall; contact with chemical, heat, electricity, or sharp edge where impact is not the event. Boundary: Falling_object is a hazard mechanism; struck_by is the impact event. Examples: struck by a pipe; hit by a falling tool.
accident_type.cut_laceration: Definition: A cut, laceration, puncture, tear, scratch, or slicing injury caused by a sharp, rough, broken, or cutting source. Include when: cut, lacerated, punctured, sliced, torn, or scratched injury is described; the specified resource is the blade, edge, shard, fragment, tool, or rough surface causing the injury; broken material creates a sharp contact event. Exclude when: crush, bruise, burn, chemical exposure, or blunt impact without cutting injury; wound/injury mentioned but no sharp/cutting mechanism is identified; medical treatment such as stitches without event mechanism. Boundary: Sharp_object is the hazard; cut_laceration is the accident event. Examples: cut by glass; lacerated by a metal edge.
accident_type.fall: Definition: A person slips, trips, stumbles, loses balance, jumps unintentionally, or falls from height or at the same level. Include when: person-fall event is described with fell/slipped/tripped/lost balance or equivalent wording; the specified resource is the ladder, platform, floor, stairs, equipment, vehicle, or surface involved in the fall; fall from equipment-related height or same-level fall caused by resource condition. Exclude when: object falls onto a person; pure object drop/struck-by event; fall is only an injury consequence and no resource-specific fall mechanism is linked. Boundary: For resource tagging, connect the fall event to the specified resource. Examples: worker fell from stairs; employee slipped off a ladder.
accident_type.collision: Definition: A crash or collision between vehicles, mobile equipment, objects, structures, or a person and a moving vehicle/object. Include when: collision, crash, hit against, ran into, struck each other, rollover impact, or traffic/mobile-equipment crash is described; the specified resource is a colliding vehicle/mobile machine/object or struck fixed object central to the collision; vehicle/mobile-equipment movement causes the collision event. Exclude when: falling object, chemical exposure, cut, burn, or caught-between event without collision mechanism; ordinary contact/touching with no crash/impact movement; static equipment failure without impact between moving bodies. Boundary: Collision often coexists with vehicle_mobile_equipment hazard when mobile equipment is involved. Examples: truck collided with another vehicle; forklift hit a structure.
accident_type.equipment_failure: Definition: Failure of a resource's intended containment, support, movement, guarding, electrical, or control function, including rupture, fracture, breakage, malfunction, detachment, uncoupling, collapse, or worn-part failure. Include when: equipment breaks, ruptures, bursts, fails, malfunctions, detaches, collapses, uncouples, jams, or loses containment; failed component directly contributes to release, movement, strike, fall, burn, shock, or other incident; the specified resource itself failed or is the failed component/pathway. Exclude when: equipment is involved but functions as intended; operator error, poor procedure, or unsafe handling without equipment malfunction/failure; unexpected movement with no failure evidence; use abnormal_movement when movement is the event. Boundary: Do not assign to every equipment resource in an accident; only the failed resource/component gets it. Examples: hose ruptured; support failed and the load dropped.
accident_type.abnormal_movement: Definition: Unexpected, uncontrolled, or unintended sliding, rolling, swinging, shifting, dropping, bouncing, moving, or displacement of a resource, load, tool, component, or material. Include when: object/tool/load/component moves unexpectedly, shifts, slides, rolls, swings, drops, rebounds, or displaces; unplanned movement causes impact, trapping, release, fall, or loss of control; the specified resource is the moving object or failed support/control that caused movement. Exclude when: intended movement during normal operation or transport; static equipment failure with no movement event; person falls without object/resource movement. Boundary: Use equipment_failure too only when failure/malfunction evidence exists. Examples: bar slid from its support; load shifted unexpectedly.
accident_type.projectile_ejection: Definition: A solid object, fragment, liquid, gas, dust, or material is expelled, ejected, launched, projected, blown out, or thrown with force. Include when: projected, ejected, expelled, shot, blown out, burst out, or thrown with force is described; pressure, rotation, rupture, explosion, or mechanical release ejects material/object; the specified resource is the projectile, source, or failed pathway of ejection. Exclude when: slow leakage, ordinary spill, gravity fall, or manual throwing without forceful ejection; object falls/drops without projection force; chemical exposure without projection/ejection wording. Boundary: Can coexist with chemical_splash or struck_by depending on what is ejected and what it hits. Examples: solution was projected; fragment was ejected from the machine.
accident_type.chemical_exposure: Definition: A person is exposed to a chemical through skin/eye contact, inhalation, ingestion, splash, spray, vapor, fumes, mist, or other body exposure route. Include when: chemical reaches, contacts, is inhaled by, splashes onto, sprays onto, or affects a person; human exposure outcome is described, even if injury severity is not fully detailed; the specified resource is the chemical source, released substance, or failed pathway causing exposure. Exclude when: chemical is present, stored, transferred, or leaked without human exposure evidence; exposure is to heat, electricity, dust, or biological material without chemical substance evidence; PPE, shower, eyewash, hospital, or response resource is only used after the exposure. Boundary: chemical_contact_hazard is the hazard pathway; chemical_exposure is the accident event/outcome. Examples: sulfide solution reached the worker; employee inhaled chemical vapor.
